items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Bechet asked me if I would do the season with him and naturally, I accepted. ... We played Saturday afternoon and night and Sunday afternoon

ctx.x: In order to receive benefits from the social security, it was necessary to report to the bureau nearest to you, and there was one not far from where I lived. I applied and had to report for five weeks before I could get a check for 25 dollars every week for a certain length of time. One could not actually call this a benefit from the government, because a certain amount of money is taken out of one's salary every working week, and it is one's privilege to apply for and receive a certain amount when they are out…

During this procedure, Bechet, as every one called Sidney in New York, had applied for a summer session job at a place called Camp Unity which was 70 miles from New York. The Camp was run by the Communist Party, and was known to be very liberal concerning the social mixing of races. I had been aware of the existence of this camp from other musicians that had done a season there. Bechet asked me if I would do the season with him and naturally, I accepted. The regular season was for six weeks, starting the 15th of…

Bechet arranged for us to get free supper which was offered to us. The salary was 25 dollars for the weekend, room and board included from Friday evening until Sunday evening. We played Saturday afternoon and night and Sunday afternoon which gave us the opportunity to be home Sunday night.
